pages.text: Overview â Grain Developers / API Docs MCP Docs â grain.com â Overview Authentication Versions Rate Limits Endpoints Uploads Hooks 2025-10-31 Endpoints Overview Quick Start The Grain API lets you read and manage recordings, highlights, uploads, and more. This page gets you from zero to your first successful request! 1. Create a Personal Access Token A Personal Access Token (PAT) authenticates requests as you, with the same access you have in Grain. Generate one here: https://grain.com/app/settings/integrations?tab=api See Authentication for the other ways to authenticate. 2. Make Your First Request Every request needs a token in the Authorization header and a Public-Api-Version header (see Versions ). Here's Token Info , using an example token: Copy curl -X GET \ -H "Authorization: Bearer grain_pat_example123" \ -H "Public-Api-Version: 2026-10-01" \ https://api.grain.com/_/public-api/v2/token-info Copy { "type" : "personal_access_token" , "scope" : "personal" , "user_id" : "7890-abcd-ef01-2222-3456-7890ffff" , "name" : "Luke Skywalker" , "expires_at" : null } Swap in your own token and you're set. Next Steps Authentication â authentication methods, use the one that best suits your use case Versions â Grain's Public-Api-Version header explained Rate Limits â request limits and the headers returned with each response Endpoints â the full API reference Next Authentication â On this page Quick Start 1. Explore Integrations Frequently Asked Questions What is Grain? Grain is an AI notetaker and conversation intelligence platform that records video calls, Slack huddles, and in-person meetings to provide accurate summaries, insights, and coaching feedback. Unlike other notetaking tools, Grain captures all meeting content: video, desktop captured audio, and resulting transcripts and notes. We make it easy to share meaningful data with your clients and collaborators, and to transform your meeting data into actionable insights and deliverables using AI technology. Who is Grain for? Grain serves any team that relies on meetings, but we specialize in small to mid-market and enterprise sales, customer success, and product teams. These teams benefit most from automated meeting capture, call analysis, team coaching features, and AI-powered deliverables using meeting data that save time and improve collaboration. How do I use Grain with my team? Send clips, share notes, and deliver feedback to teammates with Grain's built-in Teams feature. Create groups to organize and automatically share specific meeting types with exactly who needs access, streamlining collaboration. ‍ How much does Grain cost? Grain is free forever for individuals. Pro is $15/month for one person. Business is $29 per seat/month, billed annually (2-seat minimum), and adds a shared workspace for your team. What's included in the free plan? Unlimited meetings up to 45 minutes each, 30-day history, unlimited AI notes, live transcripts, bot-free capture, and Claude & ChatGPT connections. How much time do I save with Grain vs. manual note-taking? On average, users save about 10 minutes per meeting by eliminating manual note-taking and follow-ups. Over a month, that's 20+ hours per team member that can be reinvested in coaching, strategy, or revenue-driving activities instead. Is Grain secure and compliant? Yes. Grain holds SOC 2 Type II. All data is hosted on AWS infrastructure in the USA within a dedicated virtual private cloud (VPC). Grain conducts annual penetration testing by third-party firms (Prescient Security) and maintains an A+ Qualys/SSL Labs rating. User authentication uses Google, Microsoft, SSO, or SAML. For more details, see https://grain.com/security . Do I need permission to record meetings with Grain? In most regions you are required to inform participants that a meeting is being recorded, and in some jurisdictions you must obtain explicit consent from all parties. Grain helps by clearly indicating when a bot is present or recording, but you remain responsible for complying with local recording and privacy laws. Does Grain share my data with AI providers? Grain uses AI models to provide its services. Neither Grain nor its subprocessors use your data for model training. See a list of our subprocessors here: https://grain.com/grain-subprocessors . ‍ Can I delete my meetings and data from Grain? Yes. You can delete individual meetings, entire sets of recordings, or your workspace data from within Grain. When you delete content, it is removed from your workspace and associated sharing targets, and Grain enforces backend deletion according to its data retention and security policies. How do CRM integrations work? Grain integrates with Salesforce, HubSpot, Pipedrive, and other leading CRMs to automatically sync meeting summaries, transcripts, and insights to deal records. See how each integration works at https://grain.com/integrations . How does Grain compare to competitors like Fathom, Gong, or tl;dv? Grain offers simple, transparent pricing starting at $15/month with no hidden fees or contracts. Unlike enterprise-heavy alternatives, Grain delivers powerful conversation intelligence at a fraction of typical costs while maintaining ease of use and fast deployment. Why should we transcribe our meetings? Transcripts create a searchable record of work completed in meetings, which AI then converts into actionable summaries. Without transcripts, meeting outcomes remain invisible to the organization, creating inefficiencies in follow-up and institutional knowledge sharing. What languages does Grain support? Grain supports over 130 languages for meeting transcription and AI notes. Common languages like English, Spanish, French, German, Italian, Portuguese, and Japanese deliver the highest accuracy with speaker recognition and punctuation. Over 100 additional languages including Arabic, Hebrew, and Thai are also supported. Try Grain today. It’s free forever. Capture every meeting. Enrich your transcripts. Feed your AI. pages.title: Authentication â Grain Developers
pages.text: Authentication â Grain Developers / API Docs MCP Docs â grain.com â Overview Authentication Versions Rate Limits Endpoints Uploads Hooks 2025-10-31 Endpoints Authentication Authenticating Calls To authenticate API calls, the client must add the following header: Copy Authorization : Bearer TOKEN where TOKEN is obtained by one of the methods below. Token Types There are three types of tokens which can have one of two access scopes. Type Scope Personal Access Token ( PAT ) personal Generated manually from the integrations page . Doesn't expire, and can be revoked at any time. Workspace Access Token ( WAT ) workspace Generated manually from the integrations page . Doesn't expire, and can be revoked at any time. OAuth Token personal , workspace Issued through the OAuth2 Flow . Expires, must be refreshed. Scope personal Provides the same access level as the user who authorized the token. workspace Provides FULL DATA ACCESS of the workspace. Can be generated by workspace admins only. NOTE: The workspace scope is not available on all plans. Check https://grain.com/pricing to see if your plan includes Workspace API. Tokens with the personal scope, including Personal Access Tokens, also authenticate the Grain MCP server at https://api.grain.com/_/mcp . Tokens with the workspace scope are not accepted by the MCP server. OAuth2 Flow This authentication method is for developers building integrations with Grain to be used by any Grain users. The API supports a standard OAuth2 Authorization Code flow, including the PKCE extension for client-side only authentication. At least one redirect URI is required to register a new client. For browser-based client applications, a list of CORS origins can also be added. Authorization Code Step 1 Obtain the client_id and client_secret (only for server-side applications) credentials. Step 2 Open the url https://grain.com/_/public-api/oauth2/authorize with the following query params. Param client_id Obtained separately in Step 1 redirect_uri Must exactly match a registered redirect URI. On localhost , 127.0.0.1 and [::1] , any port matches response_type Must be code state Optional. Grain returns it unchanged in Step 4 . PKCE already protects the flow, so state is only needed if your client relies on it code_challenge A random string, hashed with SHA256 and base64 URL encoded code_challenge_method Must be S256 scopes personal or workspace . Defaults to personal Step 3 If the user is not already signed in to Grain, they will be prompted to sign in. After being authenticated, the user will be prompted to confirm the OAuth2 connection. Step 4 The user will be redirected to redirect_uri from Step 2 with the code query param, and state if you sent one. Step 5 Make a POST request to generate the token. See OAuth2 Generate Token Diagram sequenceDiagram participant you as You actor user as User participant grain as Grain Note right of you: Step 1 you-->>grain: Request Client ID & Secret (manually) grain-->>you: Client ID & Secret Note right of you: Step 2 user->>you: Requests OAuth you->>user: Open or Redirects to oauth2/authorize user->>grain: oauth2/authorize Note left of grain: Step 3 grain->>user: Requests login user->>grain: Login grain->>user: Requests Confirm OAuth user->>grain: Confirms Note left of grain: Step 4 grain->>user: Redirects to redirect_uri w/code user->>you: redirect_uri w/code Note right of you: Step 5 you->>grain: POST oauth2/token w/code grain->>you: access_token & refresh_token Note right of you: Refresh you->>grain: POST oauth2/token w/refresh_token grain->>you: access_token & refresh_token Client ID Metadata Document Public clients, such as MCP clients and native apps, can skip Step 1 by using an HTTPS URL as their client_id . That URL must serve a JSON Client ID Metadata Document describing the client. Copy { "client_id" : "https://app.example.com/oauth/client.json" , "client_name" : "Example App" , "redirect_uris" : [ "https://app.example.com/oauth/callback" ] , "grant_types" : [ "authorization_code" , "refresh_token" ] , "response_types" : [ "code" ] , "token_endpoint_auth_method" : "none" } Field client_id Required. Must exactly match the URL the document is served from redirect_uris Required. The redirect_uri in Step 2 must exactly match one of these client_name Shown to the user when they confirm the connection. Defaults to the URL's host grant_types Must include authorization_code . Add refresh_token to receive refresh tokens response_types Must be code if present token_endpoint_auth_method Must be none if present. Client secrets are not supported Grain applies these rules to documents and their clients: The URL must use https and serve the document directly, with no redirects, in at most 5 KB. Grain caches the document for the max-age in its Cache-Control header, between 5 minutes and 24 hours, and revalidates it with its ETag . PKCE is required, so send code_challenge in Step 2 and code_verifier when generating the token. http redirect URIs are only allowed on localhost , 127.0.0.1 and [::1] , where any port matches. The workspace scope is only available to clients verified by Grain. Refresh Token After the access_token has expired, you may generate a new one. See OAuth2 Refresh Token â Previous Overview Next Versions â On this page Authenticating Calls Token Types OAuth2 Flow Authorization Code Client ID Metadata Document Refresh Token

Status Each version has a status describing its state in the lifecycle. Status current Current Version. New features and endpoints are added to this version only. deprecated Still live, but will move to sunsetting. sunsetting Will be sunset on the specified date. Rate-limits to this version will be gradually reduced. retired No longer supported, requests using this version will error. pages.title: Rate Limits â Grain Developers
pages.text: Rate Limits â Grain Developers / API Docs MCP Docs â grain.com â Overview Authentication Versions Rate Limits Endpoints Uploads Hooks 2025-10-31 Endpoints Rate Limits Overview Grain rate limits requests with a token bucket algorithm per auth token. Requests beyond the bucket's current balance return a 429 Too Many Requests . Limits Bucket capacity 30 requests Refill rate 2 req/sec In Practice Sustained traffic 120 req/min Burst from full bucket 30 requests Time to refill empty bucket 15 seconds NOTE: Rate limits for sunsetting versions are gradually reduced. See Versions . Headers Grain also returns the following headers with every request: Header x-ratelimit-limit Bucket capacity. x-ratelimit-remaining Tokens remaining in the bucket. Retry-After * only on 429 Number of seconds you must wait before the bucket has a token available again. â Previous Versions Next Endpoints â On this page Overview Headers

Param Type before_datetime ISO8601 formatted timestamp 2026-01-01T09:30:00Z Only return recordings which start_datetime is after the selected date (exclusive) after_datetime ISO8601 formatted timestamp 2026-01-01T09:30:00Z Only return recordings which start_datetime is before the selected date (inclusive) attendance only for personal scope One of: - hosted - attended hosted Only return recordings where the user was the meeting host. attended Only return recordings where the user attended the meeting. participant_scope One of: - internal - external internal Only return recordings of internal / team meetings. external Only return recordings of external / customer meetings. title_search string Only return recordings which title matches the given search string. team uuid Only return recordings which team matches the given team id. Meeting type ids can be found through the List Meeting Types endpoint.
